name: fadvise64_64
synopsis: long fadvise64_64(int fd, off_t offset, off_t len, int advice);
description: The fadvise64_64 system call allows programs to advise the kernel about the expected access pattern of file data, enabling optimizations such as read-ahead or page caching.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting offset of the region to which the advice applies.

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the region, or 0 to indicate until the end of the file.

parameters.name: advice
parameters.description: Advice value indicating the access pattern, such as POSIX_FADV_NORMAL or POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL.

return_value.failure: Returns an error number on error

errors.description: The fd argument was not a valid file descriptor.
An invalid value was specified for advice.
The specified file descriptor refers to a pipe or FIFO.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.6, if len was specified as 0, it was interpreted as zero bytes instead of until the end of the file.
versions: Linux 2.5.60 and later, with architecture-specific variants like fadvise64_64 since Linux 2.6.14 on ARM
